title: Product Thinking & Problem Framing
summary: Connect user problems, context, desired outcomes, and solution assumptions.

levelDescriptors.text: You have not yet distinguished problems, solutions, features, and outcomes.
You can explain the user, a general problem, and the desired outcome.
You can create a problem statement and identify assumptions with guidance.
You can independently frame a problem using evidence, scope, constraints, and outcomes.
You have evidence that your framing influenced a product decision and can explain the trade-offs.

title: User Discovery
summary: Collect and synthesize evidence about user needs and behavior.

levelDescriptors.text: You have not yet learned the purpose of user research.
You understand interviews, observations, pain points, and insights.
You have conducted simple research using a guide or template.
You can independently plan, conduct, and synthesize user research.
You have research evidence that changed a product priority, design, or decision.

title: Product Strategy
summary: Define target users, value, outcomes, constraints, and strategic choices.

levelDescriptors.text: You have not yet learned how user value, business value, and product direction connect.
You can explain vision, target users, value proposition, and outcomes.
You can create a simple strategy brief and justify a focus area.
You can independently connect insights, positioning, outcomes, constraints, and choices.
You have evidence that a strategy was used to select, reject, or change a real initiative.

title: Prioritization
summary: Choose problems and initiatives using impact, evidence, effort, and trade-offs.

levelDescriptors.text: You usually prioritize based on preference or request order.
You understand impact, effort, urgency, evidence, and trade-offs.
You have used a prioritization framework with guidance.
You can independently prioritize and explain trade-offs to a team.
You have evidence that a prioritization decision produced learning or a measurable outcome.

title: Requirements & Roadmapping
summary: Translate problems into testable requirements and an outcome-based sequence of work.

levelDescriptors.text: You have not yet written requirements or a roadmap.
You understand problem statements, user stories, acceptance criteria, milestones, and roadmaps.
You can write simple requirements and a roadmap using a template.
You can independently create testable requirements and an outcome-based roadmap.
You have artifacts used across functions and updated using new evidence or context.

title: Product Analytics & Experimentation
summary: Define success metrics, interpret evidence, and test product assumptions.

levelDescriptors.text: You have not yet learned how product success is measured.
You understand metrics, baselines, targets, funnels, and hypotheses.
You can define a simple metric or experiment plan with guidance.
You can independently create a measurement plan, interpret results, and decide what to do next.
You have an experiment or analysis that changed a real product decision.

title: Stakeholder Communication
summary: Align people around context, decisions, risks, and expectations.

levelDescriptors.text: You find it difficult to explain context, decisions, or needs to others.
You can communicate basic status and ideas in a structured way.
You can create updates, presentations, or decision memos with guidance.
You can align different perspectives, handle disagreement, and document decisions.
You have evidence that your communication resolved conflict or accelerated an important decision.

title: Cross-Functional Execution
summary: Coordinate design, engineering, and other partners until a product outcome is delivered.

levelDescriptors.text: You have not yet coordinated work across different functions.
You understand the roles of product, design, engineering, and delivery rituals.
You have worked on a cross-functional project with guidance.
You can independently manage dependencies, risks, decisions, and follow-up.
You have evidence of a completed cross-functional project with reflection and measurable learning or outcomes.
